{{Current events header|2016|02|16}}

<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Iraqi Civil War (2014–present)]]
**Three [[United States|Americans]] abducted last month in [[Baghdad]] are freed by the [[Iraqi Intelligence Service]]. [http://www.ocregister.com/articles/iraqi-704313-iraq-government.html (AP via ''Orange County Register'')]
;Arts and culture
*The jewels of former Philippine [[First Spouse of the Philippines|first lady]] [[Imelda Marcos]] are to be auctioned. Valued at $21 million (USD), they were seized by the [[Government of the Philippines|government]] when her husband [[Ferdinand Marcos]] was overthrown. [http://www.cnn.com/2016/02/16/luxury/imelda-marcos-jewelery-auction/ (CNN)], [http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-35583699 (BBC)]
* After more then 200 years, [[Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart|Mozart's]] and [[Antonio Salieri|Salieri's]] lost [[cantata]] ''Per la Ricuperata Salute di Ofelia'' is discovered in [[Prague]]. [http://www.reuters.com/article/us-czech-mozart-idUSKCN0VP1PQ (Reuters)], [http://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/mozart-wolfgang-amadeus-antonio-salieri-lorenzo-da-ponte-libretto-a6873481.html (The Independent)], [http://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-35589422 (BBC)]

;International relations
*Former [[Secretary-General of the United Nations|U.N. Secretary-General]] [[Boutros Boutros-Ghali]] (1992-96) of [[Egypt]] has died. He was 93.  [http://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2016-02-16/urgent-un-announces-death-of-former-un-chief-boutros-boutros-ghali (AP via Bloomberg)]
*[[Cuba–United States relations]]
**The [[United States]] and [[Cuba]] sign an agreement restoring [[Airline|commercial air traffic]] between the two countries for the first time in 50 years. The [[United States Department of Transportation|U.S. Department of Transportation]] immediately opened bidding for as many as 110 U.S.-Cuba flights per day to [[Havana]] and nine other destinations. Travel from the U.S. is permitted in   12 authorized categories, which does not include [[tourism]]. [http://bigstory.ap.org/article/38bd18dd7e8449cebdcece9115962457/us-cuba-sign-deal-commercial-flights (AP)] [http://www.jamaicaobserver.com/news/US-authorizes-up-to-110-daily-flights-to-Cuba (AFP via ''The Jamaica Observer'')]

;Law and crime
*Four [[United States|American]] [[journalist]]s are charged by [[Bahrain]] for  "unlawful obstruction of vehicles and attending unlawful gatherings." The state-run [[Bahrain News Agency]] said all were released "pending further investigations." [[Freelancer|Freelance]] reporter Anna Day and a [[film crew]], who were covering the fifth anniversary of the [[Arab Spring]] [[Bahraini uprising of 2011|uprisings]], are scheduled to fly to [[Dubai]] tonight. [http://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/bahrain-charges-releases-anna-day-3-other-american-journalists-n519291 (NBC News)] [http://www.nydailynews.com/news/world/american-journalists-arrested-bahrain-charged-released-article-1.2533077 (''New York Daily News'')]
